title: Dimension of an effective Cartier divisor on an integral scheme
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $X$ be an integral scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme] of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] with $\dim X=d\ge 1$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], and let $D\hookrightarrow X$ be a nonempty effective Cartier divisor [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal]. Then $\dim D=d-1$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension].

source.place: Tag 0BEV proof, after constructing Z(s): the effective Cartier zero scheme has codimension 1 and dimension d-1

proof.text: Because $X$ is integral, every nonempty affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ is integral, so $A$ is a domain. The finite-type hypothesis makes $A$ a finitely generated $k$-algebra. The existing equality of dimensions for nonempty affine opens of an integral locally finite-type scheme, [lem-sc-integral-locally-algebraic-affine-opens-dimension], shows that all nonempty affine opens have the same dimension; since $X$ is covered by them and the Krull dimension of a space is the supremum of the dimensions of the members of an open cover (Stacks Tag 0055, elementary from [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]: a chain of irreducible closed subsets meets an open containing the generic point of its smallest member in a chain of the same length), this common value is $\dim X=d$, so $\dim U=d$.

source.place: Tag 0BEV proof, dimension theory as in Lemma lemma-dimension-locally-algebraic

proof.text: On an affine chart meeting the nonempty effective Cartier divisor $D$, its ideal is generated by a nonzerodivisor $f$. Since the chart ring $A$ is a domain, $f$ is nonzero; since the chart meets $D$, it is not a unit. The affine quotient chart is therefore $\operatorname{Spec}(A/(f))$, and [lem-sc-effective-cartier-affine-dimension-drop] gives dimension $d-1$.

source.place: Tag 0BEV proof, after constructing Z(s): the effective Cartier zero scheme has codimension one

proof.text: The nonempty affine quotient charts cover $D$, and each has dimension $d-1$ by step 2. By the definition of Krull dimension as the supremum of dimensions of local chains, the dimension of a scheme covered by affine opens is the supremum of the dimensions of those opens; hence $\dim D=d-1$.
